decisions.reason: As a multi-item dietary supplement range that supports the firm's consumer-health portfolio expansion and was still prominently presented after launch, it is more likely to be retained than withdrawn.
This skin-and-hair supplement fits the pharmacy-oriented consumer-health strategy, though the crowded category makes it somewhat easier to discontinue if demand is weaker than expected.
A joint-health supplement suits the firm's established pharmacy customer base and aging-health demand, so a launch that gained its own page would usually be kept.
The immune supplement was explicitly marketed as innovative and fits the firm's expansion in consumer health, which lowers the likelihood of a near-term withdrawal.

Despite the 2018 valsartan-related issue, a generic blood-pressure medicine still matches the firm's prescription and generics capabilities, so management would more likely fix supply and quality issues than exit the product.
An over-the-counter migraine triptan fits the firm's OTC and pharmacy strengths and, as a relatively recent launch, would normally be given more time to establish itself.
